ideas.description: Diagnostic run offline in drafts/. The submission does not change. Several later decisions (H7.1.1, H6.4.1) depend on how real the tip's 0.07 pp margin is. Load the E058 commit (fb3f626) through the benchmark's own build/prepare/train/eval code path, after one build, and run 10 extra trials on seeds 3-12. Report per-seed accuracy, the mean, the per-seed sd and the per-trial train time. If budget allows (~1 min of GPU after build), also run the E061 commit (block-1 freeze at 0.7) on the same seeds 3-12. That gives a paired estimate of the 0.7-vs-0.8 freeze cost that does not depend on seeds 0-2. Keep the commits, data and eval path unchanged, and do not touch anything the timed harness uses. Record the result in the notebook as evidence for H4.1.2 (and H4.1.6 for the paired sd).
ideas.expected: No metric change, since the submission is untouched. Prediction: per-seed sd 0.12-0.25 pp. Extra-seed mean 0.7520-0.7545, point ~0.7530, about 0.05 pp below the seeds 0-2 mean because the keep/discard ratchet selected on those seeds. E061 minus E058 paired on seeds 3-12: -0.05 to -0.15 pp. Decision rule: mean >= 0.7535 → run the time cuts (H7.1.1, H6.4.1) next. Mean <= 0.7525 (refutes H4.1.2) → run the margin-recovery ideas (OLS, Polar Express coefficients, BN-bias x32) before any further time cut, and lower H6.4.1's priority.

ideas.description: Anneal block 1 before an earlier freeze, combining with E061's near-miss (freeze at 0.7, -0.11 pp, infeasible by 0.04). Base: E058 (fb3f626). Make one change: between samples 0.6 and 0.7 of training (162000 → 236250), multiply block 1's per-step lr by a factor that falls linearly from 1 to 0. This applies to both block-1 Muon lrs (the 128x1152 and 128x216 shape groups) and to block-1 BN-bias lrs in the SGD group. Then, from sample 236250, switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair (E061's switch point, with the same straddling-step split). Pass the block-1 multiplier as its own 0-d GPU tensor, filled each step, into the batched Muon step and the SGD param group, so nothing recompiles. Every other group keeps its schedule, and momentum buffers keep accumulating. Lookahead is unchanged, so the slow block-1 weights converge onto the now-still fast weights. Reuse E061's partial-shape warmups (channels_last, exact timed layout). Run debug_nan.py on the modified Muon step and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time 4.53-4.61 s, point ~4.57 s (-2.7% vs 4.696). Compute is identical to E061, because the anneal window still runs full steps. Accuracy 0.7515-0.7555, point ~0.7535: it should recover most of E061's -0.11 pp because block 1's last fast iterates are no longer noisy at freeze time. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best, then try the same anneal with a 0.6 freeze. Within 0.05 pp of E061: abrupt stopping was not the cost, so refute H7.1 and close earlier-freeze tuning at 0.8.

ideas.description: Math-preserving systems change: Gram Newton-Schulz in the batched compiled Muon step. Base: E058. For each stacked group X (out x in, out < in, aspect ~9), compute R = X X^T once (rectangular GEMM, bf16 inputs, fp32 accumulate). Run the 3 quintic iterations entirely in out x out space with fp32 square matmuls. Same coefficients (a,b,c): A_k = Q_k R Q_k^T (equal to Q_k^2 R, since Q is a polynomial in R), P_k = aI + bA_k + cA_k^2, Q_{k+1} = P_k Q_k, starting from Q_0 = I. Finally compute X_3 = Q_3 X with one rectangular GEMM. Keep the pre-NS Frobenius normalization, the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, the weight-norm projection, the lr and everything else identical, in both Muon variants (with and without block 1). Gate in drafts/ before launching: (1) on real momentum matrices from seed 0 at steps 0, 100 and the end, max |X_gram - X_ns3| / max|X_ns3| < 2e-2 per group; (2) drafts/time_muon.py shows a Muon GPU time saving >= 0.25 ms/step. Launch only if both pass. Re-warm both Muon variants in build() and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
ideas.expected: Muon GPU time falls from ~1.43 to ~1.05-1.2 ms/step: 2 rectangular GEMMs instead of 6, ~40% fewer NS FLOPs. Mean time -0.8% to -2.0%, point -1.3% (~4.635 s). Accuracy within ±0.08 pp of 0.7537, tighter than re-draw, because the data/RNG stream is unchanged and the update matches to rounding. Keep if feasible and >=1% faster, since the saving is deterministic and pre-measured (the E051 precedent). If the gate shows <0.25 ms, mark H2.4.8 refuted without a run: NS GEMMs are not where Muon time goes.

ideas.description: Online Label Smoothing replaces uniform LS 0.2. Base: E058. Make one change to the loss. Keep a 100x100 fp32 GPU matrix S (column c = soft target for class c), reset in prepare() to the LS-0.4 matrix (0.6 on the diagonal + 0.4/100 everywhere), plus an accumulator S_acc and counts, zeroed. Training target for a sample of class y: t = 0.5*onehot(y) + 0.5*S[:, y]. At initialization this is exactly LS 0.2, so behaviour is unchanged until the first swap. Inside the compiled step, with no data-dependent branch, add softmax(logits.detach().float()) * correct_mask into S_acc's column y with index_add_ / scatter_add, and add correct_mask to counts. At every half-epoch boundary (picked in Python by samples seen, between steps), set S = S_acc / counts.clamp_min(1). Keep the old column for any class with count 0, then zero S_acc and counts. Pass S, S_acc and counts as tensor inputs, so nothing recompiles. Accumulation runs in every resolution stage and freeze variant. Re-warm all train variants in build() on synthetic data and run debug_nan.py. Eval is unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.30 to +0.40 pp, point +0.05 pp. Superclass-structured targets add per-step signal, but 6.75 epochs gives only ~12 swaps of a noisy S (H1.11.1's named failure mode). Time +0.1% to +0.6% (one 1536x100 scatter-add per step). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.11.1 and banks margin for H6.4.1 or the 0.7 freeze. Within ±0.15 pp: class-structured soft targets are flat like uniform LS, so close H1.11. A drop >=0.25 pp refutes it, since the early S is too noisy at this horizon.

ideas.description: Stronger whitening at the same update norm and no extra cost: swap the fixed quintic coefficients (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used in all 3 NS iterations for three per-iteration Polar Express triples. Compute them with optimal_composition(num_iters=3, l=ℓ) from arxiv 2505.16932, where ℓ is the 5th-percentile smallest-singular-value ratio measured in drafts/ on the tip's real normalized momentum matrices (seed 0, steps 0/100/end, all groups). Apply the published safety scaling and do not truncate a longer list. After NS, rescale each group's output to the Frobenius norm the current NS3 output would have. Compute this cheaply as a per-group constant measured in drafts/, or online as the ratio of norms if that is cheap, so only the spectrum shape changes and the step size does not. Base: E058; everything else is unchanged. Gate in drafts/: the fraction of singular values >0.5 after the new NS must be >= NS3's, and the max singular value must be <= 1.3. Re-warm both Muon variants and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.30 to +0.35 pp, point +0.05 pp. E065 showed whitening strength matters steeply below the default, but E017 (NS5 ≈ NS3) suggests the top side is near saturation. Time unchanged (±0.5%; same number of bmm). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.2.7 and banks margin. Within ±0.15 pp: the update geometry is saturated in every direction, so close H1.2.7 and treat the H1 update branch as finished. If the gate fails (NS3 already lifts >= as many directions), retire it without a run.

ideas.description: Cash in E063's shallow epoch slope. Run only if the H4.1.2 extra-seed mean is >= 0.7535, or after a keep that banks >= +0.1 pp (H7.1.1, OLS, Polar Express). Base: the then-tip, else E058. Make one change: total epochs 6.75 → 6.5, with the 0.25 epoch removed from the 32 px stage. The 20 px (0-1.5) and 28 px (1.5-3.5) boundaries stay fixed in samples. The block-1 freeze stays at 0.8 of the new total samples (260000), and the lr warmup/decay, Muon multiplier and lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp are scaled to samples seen. The final half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation (E006/E018 practice). Warm up every new partial shape at the moved freeze switch and the new run end for each graph variant, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time 4.49-4.58 s, point ~4.53 s (-3.5%). Accuracy 0.7510-0.7545, point ~0.7530 (-0.07 pp at E063's ~0.3 pp/epoch). That is a coin flip at the gate on E058, which is why it is conditional on banked margin. A drop <=0.1 pp supports H6.4.1 (the cheapest time lever left), so keep it if feasible. A drop >=0.25 pp restores the steep-slope picture: E063 was noise, so refute H6.4.1 and stop epoch trimming.

ideas.description: Partial block-2 freeze. Base: E058 (or the H7.1.1 successor). For the last 10% of samples (from 303750, i.e. 6.075 epochs), use a new 32 px train variant that is the block-1-frozen graph plus a detached weight for block 2's first conv only (conv(x, w.detach()) behind a Python flag fixed at trace time). Block 2's later convs, all of block 3 and block-2 BN biases keep training. Pair it with a Muon variant that excludes the 128x1152 block-1 groups and block 2's 384x1152 first-conv group (its own shape group, so it drops out cleanly). Block 2's first-conv dgrad is already skipped once block 1 is frozen, so this removes its wgrad (~300 GFLOP fwd-equivalent at 15x15, bs 1536) plus one NS group. Split the straddling step at 303750 into the two partial shapes. Warm up the new train and Muon variants and every partial shape in build() with channels_last tensors (E035). Run debug_nan.py and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.
ideas.expected: Time -0.6% to -1.6%, point -1.0% (~4.65 s). Accuracy -0.25 to +0.10 pp, point -0.08 pp. Its input is frozen, so this conv has less left to learn than E062's whole block 2. Keep only if feasible and >=1% faster. A drop >=0.25 pp (like E062) means all of block 2 is still learning at 0.9, so refute H7.3 and close freezing beyond block 1.

ideas.description: Margin-recovery probe on the last untested SGD-group setting. Base: E058. Change only the BatchNorm-bias lr multiplier, from x64 to x32 (relative to the current x1.5-scaled SGD base lr), and double the BN-bias wd so lr*wd stays constant. The head (x2, wd halved), whitening bias, Muon, lookahead, curriculum, freeze, jitter and epochs are all unchanged. structured_output.summary:
The queue was empty (every idea from I001 to I084 is done or dropped), so I added 8 new ideas.

**Exploit (5):**
- **H4.1.2, priority 4:** an offline check on seeds 3-12 of E058, plus a paired E061 if budget allows. It decides whether the tip's 0.07 pp margin is real, and it gates the time cuts.
- **H7.1.1, priority 4:** combines E061's near-miss with FreezeOut. Block 1's lr ramps down linearly to 0 between 0.6 and 0.7 of training, then the existing freeze takes over at 0.7. Expected about -2.7% time with E061's accuracy loss mostly recovered.
- **H2.4.8, priority 3:** Gram Newton-Schulz, the same math with 2 instead of 6 rectangular GEMMs. Expected about -1.3% time, gated in drafts/ on matching outputs and a measured saving of at least 0.25 ms/step.
- **H6.4.1, priority 3:** cut to 6.5 total epochs, run only once margin is banked.
- **H7.3.1, priority 2:** freeze only block 2's first conv for the last 10% of samples. Expected about -1% time.

**Explore (3), each aimed at recovering margin at no time cost:**
- **H1.11.1, priority 3:** Online Label Smoothing, set up so it starts out exactly equal to LS 0.2.
- **H1.2.7, priority 3:** Polar Express per-iteration coefficients with the update norm matched to the current NS3 output. This is the only update-geometry direction E065 leaves open.
- **H1.7.4, priority 2:** BN-bias lr x32.

No queued ideas needed dropping. One bookkeeping fix for the tree: H1.6.6 is still listed as open (confidence 0.6), but I075's gate note already refuted it. Every edit pair differed per seed, and all edits reached the timed path. It should be marked refuted, and H1/H1.2/H1.6 should drop the "compile no-op" caveat.
